title: perf-bench-scratch - latency & throughput runs
content:
Notes / scratchpad for recent latency & throughput experiments (personal log)

Overview:
- Goal: measure p50/p95 latency and sustained tokens/sec for open-7B quantized variant on our Dedicated pool. Explore batching, KV-cache warmup, and quantization impact.
- Environment: dev-instance-a100-1 (A100 40GB), CUDA 12.1, pytorch 2.2 + Triton-backed runtime.
- Harness: local perf_runner.py (simple request generator, reports tokens/sec and latency distribution).

Run metadata (scripts used):
- baseline run (no batching):
  python perf_runner.py --model open-7B-8bit --seq 512 --batch 1 --iters 300 --device cuda:0 --profile out/baseline.json
- batching sweep:
  python perf_runner.py --model open-7B-8bit --seq 512 --batch {1,2,4,8,16} --iters 500 --device cuda:0 --profile out/batch-{B}.json
- kv-cache warmup test:
  python perf_runner.py --model open-7B-8bit --seq 1024 --batch 1 --iters 200 --warmup_prefix true --profile out/kv-warm.json

Raw observations (selected):
1) Baseline (batch=1, seq=512, temperature default):
   - p50 latency: 85 ms / token (inference-only, measured token emission)
   - p95 latency: 210 ms / token
   - sustained tokens/sec: ~11.8 tok/s (single stream)
   - notes: fairly noisy p95 spikes when background GC kicks in (python memory fragmentation).

2) Batching sweep (seq=512):
   batch=1  => p50 85 ms,   p95 210 ms,  tok/s 11.8
   batch=2  => p50 48 ms,   p95 120 ms,  tok/s 23.1
   batch=4  => p50 26 ms,   p95 65 ms,   tok/s 42.5
   batch=8  => p50 18 ms,   p95 40 ms,   tok/s 70.2
   batch=16 => p50 15 ms,   p95 36 ms,   tok/s 120.0 (saturation signs: higher GPU mem pressure, small tail latency improvement)
   - quick takeaway: batching gives large throughput uplift; sweet spot for latency-sensitive workloads seems 4-8 for this hardware.

3) KV-cache warmup (seq=1024, single stream):
   - cold-run p50 (first request): 140 ms/token, p95 360 ms/token
   - after 5 warmup iterations (same prefix): p50 72 ms/token, p95 160 ms/token
   - sustained tok/s after warm: ~18 tok/s (higher than baseline due to cache reuse)
   - note: cost of cache population is real for long-form generation; consider background pre-warming for high-SLA flows.

4) Quantization variants (quick A/B):
   - 8-bit (current): p50 85 ms/token, tok/s 11.8
   - 4-bit (experimental): p50 70 ms/token, tok/s 14.2, slight quality regression on long-tail tokens (manual spot-check)
   - TPU-like optimized kernel (not available here) might further reduce tail latency.

Micro-profiling notes (from perf traces):
- Top time sinks: attention kernel + KV read under high sequence lengths.
- Memory copies: some syncs on host->device noted when using streaming output path. Investigate async transfer path.
- Small overhead: request serialization (JSON) contributing ~1-2 ms per request during high qps; consider binary protocol for ultra-low-latency routes.

Simple ascii chart (throughput vs batch):
  tok/s |
  140  -|
  120  -|        *
  100  -|       *
   80  -|      *
   60  -|    *
   40  -|  *
   20  -|*
    0  -+----------------
        1 2 4 8 16  (batch)
  values approx: [11.8,23.1,42.5,70.2,120.0]

Open questions / TODOs:
- Re-run with production runtime (non-dev build) to ensure no debug overhead.
- Try hybrid batching (micro-batching + continuous batching) - look into config in serving-runtime PR #412.
- Run end-to-end latency (including network hop + router) to capture real-world p95.
- Evaluate 4-bit model on a longer eval set for quality regressions (tie to eval harness).
- Investigate host->device async memcpy changes (profiling points above).

Quick decisions / recommendations (working):
- For API route with <200ms p95 SLO: target batch 4-8, prefer KV-warm prefixes where possible, and enable async transfer path.
- For high-throughput internal pipelines: set batch up to 16 and accept slightly higher p95 tail but much lower cost/token.

Log entries (timestamps):
- 2026-02-18 09:10: initial baseline run (saved out/baseline.json)
- 2026-02-20 15:35: batching sweep (saved out/batch-*.json), observed 8x throughput improvement vs batch=1 on aggregated metric
- 2026-02-25 11:00: kv-cache warmup test (saved out/kv-warm.json), confirmed warmup benefit ~2x vs cold

Notes to self: keep this doc as scratchpad. After we stabilize settings, port key numbers to console/rollouts dashboard and add to perf-bench canonical doc.

References / links: see linked_artifacts above (PR with batching change, confluence draft for perf policies, JIRA infra tickets).

-- Jordan
